### Step 1 : Create the Project

* Under GAMES, create a new empty project and select Blueprint

  ![][image1]


### Step 2 : Create the Level

* Create a new Basic Level  
* Make sure to save the Level 


  ![][image2]![][image3]![][image4]


  **❗❗ Remember to save & name your Level ❗❗**


### Step 3 : Create your Assets

🌄 Background & Props

* You can download and add them into your project from these links  
  - [https://www.fab.com](https://www.fab.com/)  
    - [https://sketchfab.com](https://sketchfab.com)

### Step 4 : Create the Camera Actor

	**\*\* Both Cine Camera & the normal camera actor works fine \*\***

* Click on the plus icon, under **Place Actors** hover over **Cinematic** and select **Cine Camera Actor**

  ![][image5]


* To create a normal camera actor, you need to find it from **All** ➡ **Camera Actor**

  **![][image6]**


* Set up the Camera’s Aspect Ratio base from the image below

  ![][image7]


* In default, **Cine Camera Actor** and **Camera Actor** aspect ratio should be Standard Landscape size

  If you want to change the Cine Camera Actor’s aspect ratio to phone aspect ratio, you may refer to this link 


  


  


  


  

* If you are using the Cine Camera

  <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/u-260laYyoo?si=wY1YI_bkKfuo0MFq" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>


  ![][image8]


* If you are using the normal Camera Actor

  ![][image9]


  …you can also type in the aspect ratio as “9 x 16” or “9:16”

### Step 5 : Connecting the Camera to the Level Blueprint

![][image10]

👆 This is what you should be aiming for 👆

Set View Target with Blend

- a node for switching the view from a target (in this case “get player controller”) into a new view target (in this case “CineCameraActor”)

  CineCameraActor 

  - can be dragged from viewport into the blueprint

    SET : Show Mouse Cursor 

  - is to force the mouse to be in the screen all the time
